title: Baltimore Officers Fire Multiple Rounds After Suspect Pulls Gun
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Baltimore, Maryland — On Tuesday, February 24, 2026, at approximately 6:15 p.m., officers with the Baltimore Police Department (BPD) were in a store in the 3600 block of Belair Road when they observed an adult male, later identified 37-year-old Dwight Hawkins, who they believed to be armed. Officers saw Hawkins exit the store and began to follow him. Hawkins began to run from the officers. Officers gave the man multiple commands. As Hawkins continued to run, he pulled out a handgun, coming in close proximity to one of the officers. Two officers fired their service weapons, striking Hawkins. Officers rendered emergency medical aid until emergency medical services (EMS) arrived on scene. Hawkins was transported to a nearby hospital, where he was later pronounced dead. No officers were injured during the incident. A handgun was recovered near Hawkins. Police said that Hawkins was prohibited from owning a firearm and was also known to police officers from his "lengthy arrest record,". There were at least 16 rounds fired, but it's unclear if Hawkins fired his weapon or not.
